summary: The code does what the request asks. When a job's request names commit hashes, the producer's and the verifier's snapshots get a read-only, filtered `ATHENA-COMMITS.txt`. It is built with the same classify()/visible_to_agents() filter as HISTORY.txt. Nothing is added that links back to the user's repository: no git objects, refs, alternates or remotes. The file is listed in `.git/info/exclude`, so no candidate commit carries it. I ran the new tests and all pass: 66 athena-git tests, the two athena-context brief tests and the athena-core wiring test. The recorded CI checks for fmt, clippy and the full test suite also passed. The hash detection is a heuristic, but every hash it finds is checked against the repository (rev_parse to a commit, plus an ancestor check), and its limits are documented. The verdict is fail on criterion 7 alone: the new decision D155 calls itself an exception to "D08's rule that agents never see the real history", but D08 was not edited. It still says "agents lose `git log` of the real history. That is the point.", with no reference to D155. The accepted plan promised to reword that sentence. The fix is small: reword D08's Tradeoff line, or add an "Amended by D155" note there.
